Seeded 2026-08-15 at the live count: 28842 excess lines over the 80-line budget, 652 functions across 123 of the bundled modules, longest account.account_move_line_tax_details._get_query_tax_details at 499.

WHY THE TREE AND NOT A MODULE. pyfunclen measures odoo/ only, and until now nothing measured addons/, so excess extracted out of core into any addon left both numbers looking better. d3967e48968 is the case that exposed it: _run_action_webhook went 92 -> 57 and the 12 units it shed had to be checked by hand against addons/api_transport, because no gate could. The per-module --addon pattern cannot close this -- it only sees modules someone remembered to onboard, and the receiving module is the one nobody onboarded. One number over the whole tree has no such blind spot.

WHY no-increase AND NOT exact. Measured at four points on this branch: 27445 at -30d, 29684 at -14d, 30523 at -7d, 28842 today -- ~1700 of movement per week in both directions, over 587 commits touching addons/**/*.py in the last fortnight against core's 164. Under exact this gate would be red almost continuously and would teach reflexive --update, which is what makes a floor unauditable. One-sided keeps the property that matters here (excess cannot be relocated into this tree without failing) and drops the one it cannot hold (locking every improvement the same day it lands).

It is therefore the first ratchet invoked with --mode; coding_guidelines.rst *The ratchets* records the exception and why. Lower it whenever the tree is measured lower -- an improvement is free here, not owed.

Measured with tooling/architecture/py_function_length.py --count --addon addons at 4a3b2d5fcab, on a clean addons/ tree.
